title: Lumen bills hours already paid over x402
description: Lumen's invoice LUM-2026-10A arrives for October 1 to 15. It bills 2,140 on demand hours, but 600 of them are the spot hours Forge already paid for over x402 on October 9. Elix proposes paying $12,234.00 and disputing $1,260.00, and Sam approves it.

title: Stormvault changes its payout address
description: Two hours after Stormvault's payout address changes, Atlas asks for the full Texas 2025 radar archive for $4,800.00. Dev can approve the spend, but the money stays on hold until Priya verifies the new address.

title: Forge retries a request with a new key
description: Forge asks for 600 spot hours for $1,260.00, and its HTTP client retries 41 seconds later with a new idempotency key. Elix denies the retry as a duplicate and links it to the first request.

title: Scout tries to approve its own order
description: Scout asks for 1,200 Signalboard records for $480.00 and copies the vendor's note claiming the order is pre-approved by finance. Elix records the claim, sends the request to Maya, and refuses when Scout tries to approve it.

title: Scout splits an order into small packs
description: Scout buys Parsec query packs at $24.00 each, one every two minutes. The first six auto approve. The seventh would bring the hour to $168.00, over the $150 cap, so Elix sends it to Maya as a split purchase.

title: Sam fixes an entry in a closed month
description: Sam recodes a September Signalboard entry from 6110 to 6210. September is closed, so Elix refuses the edit and creates a correction that reverses and reposts in October. It is the third such recode, so the learner proposes a coding policy.

title: Learn approval policies from history
description: The learner reviews July to September and proposes auto approve policies where a person approved every precedent. Terrafield 3 m scenes are left out because Dev rejected one in August. Priya approves the proposals.

title: Preview the October close
description: Elix previews the October close, proposes accruals for Anthropic tokens, AWS storage and Lumen on demand hours that have not been invoiced yet, and lists what still blocks the close.

title: Jordan asks why an invoice was paid short
description: Jordan, the external auditor, asks why LUM-2026-10A was paid $1,260.00 short. The answer comes back in one query with every event, actor, rule and evidence id.

title: Try your own purchase
description: Submit any purchase as any agent, with optional price and payee overrides, and watch the checks decide.
